meta.title: Fran Barahona — Full Stack Developer
meta.description: Full stack with React, TypeScript and Rails. I lead frontend at Webel and build products where engineering and AI meet.

hero.title: Complex systems. Products people get.
hero.subtitle: I've spent about five years building web products end to end. I started full stack with Ruby on Rails; now I lead frontend at Webel with React and TypeScript. I move across architecture, interface and product, and increasingly close to AI applied to building software.
hero.scrollHint: Scroll to bring the system into order
hero.sceneLabel: Abstract visualization: a scattered cloud of nodes that reorganizes into a structured form as you scroll

webel.title: Webel
webel.intro: A home-services marketplace with millions of users. I'm the web lead: Organizations, marketplace, programmatic SEO and the internal dashboard.

areas.name: Webel Organizations
areas.description: The B2B platform for companies: employees, services, calendar, leads, client chat, tax details, service areas, schedules and payouts. A full product on its own.

areas.name: Marketplace core
areas.description: The main product: search and browsing the offer. We migrated the whole app to React. Today it's a storefront that redirects to the apps, with no login or users. On the roadmap: booking, accounts and the rest of the features.

areas.name: Programmatic SEO
areas.description: Over 50k templates built from scratch in Astro, with structured data and solid performance. Top organic result on Google for «Limpieza a domicilio en Madrid».

areas.name: Internal dashboard
areas.description: The tool the team runs operations with: users, services, incidents and business metrics.

projects.title: Things I've been building
projects.intro: Products in production, my own systems and the odd experiment. Ordered by where my energy goes now.

principles.title: Four ideas that guide me (no dogma)

items.title: Understand first, build second
items.description: Code is the cheap part. Before writing a line I ask who it's for, what problem it solves and how we'll know it works.

items.title: Complexity stays behind the curtain
items.description: A complex system is no excuse for a complex interface. My job is to absorb that and hand back something people grasp at first sight.

items.title: Pieces you can swap
items.description: Today's product won't be next year's. I build out of pieces you can replace without tearing the whole building down.

items.title: AI speeds things up; judgment stays mine
items.description: I use agents and models to explore faster, automate the repetitive and reach the decisions that matter sooner. The tool amplifies; the judgment stays mine.

skills.title: From server to pixel — and from pixel to business

experience.title: Full stack to frontend, then into product
experience.evolutionNote: Each stage has brought me closer to where engineering and product meet. What's next is that same place, amplified by AI.

contact.title: If you're building something interesting…
contact.intro: I'm drawn to teams that ship real products and to projects where engineering and product overlap. If that sounds like what you're working on, write to me.
